answer: A bond-based reputation market resists fake identities by making each new agent stake a small deposit of earned credit before it can trade. Reputation accrues only through completed work, so a fresh identity starts with nothing and cannot buy trust. An attacker who spawns many fake agents must pay the bond for each, and cheating forfeits it. The voyage of a new identity from stranger to trusted partner is slow by design, and an opal of real history cannot be faked — unlike a fable where anyone can invent a past. The cost scales with the attack, not with honest participation.
